outlier.evidence: Ratings 6, 5, 5, 4 lie within two points. Reviewer_aBu9's 6 is the only score above the threshold, but aBu9 also asked for missing ablations and baselines and kept 6 after the rebuttal. Without Reviewer_neqB (4, with two claims the paper contradicts) the mean is 5.33, still below the threshold.

inattentive_reviews.evidence: Rating 4. Its main experimental objection, that VigDet is 'compared against other methods that do not incorporate prior knowledge', is wrong: lines 246-255 and Tables 1-2 include Co-activity, Clickstream, LPA(CF/TL) and AMDN-HAGE + GNN(CF/TL), all built on prior-knowledge graphs. Its related-work objection is also wrong: Section 2.1 (lines 73-84) discusses these methods. It never replied to the rebuttal that pointed this out.

checkable_claims.claim: VigDet is compared only against methods that do not incorporate prior knowledge.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 246-255: Co-activity and Clickstream use pre-defined similarity graphs; LPA and AMDN-HAGE + GNN use the same CF and TL prior graphs as VigDet (Table 2).

checkable_claims.claim: The related-work section does not discuss existing detectors that use prior knowledge.
checkable_claims.evidence: Section 2.1 (lines 73-84) covers graph methods built on pre-defined features [5, 24, 31] and states their weakness. The discussion is short but present.

checkable_claims.claim: The improvement over AMDN-HAGE is shown on one dataset only.
checkable_claims.evidence: Tables 1-2 use only the IRA dataset. The COVID data in Section 5.2 has no labels (lines 290-292). Reviewer_oo8n in B made the same point.

checkable_claims.claim: No ablation shows what is lost without the prior-knowledge graph.
checkable_claims.evidence: VigDet starts from AMDN-HAGE + KMeans (lines 212-215). Table 1 reports that start at AP 82.0, VigDet-E (one E-step on the prior graph) at 85.1 (CF) and 85.5 (TL), and VigDet at 87.2 and 86.1. The paper does not call this an ablation. The authors said so in the rebuttal; q2wM did not reply.

checkable_claims.claim: The 'temporal logic' prior is one simple inequality that removes some account pairs.
checkable_claims.evidence: Eq. 5 (lines 164-167) counts a co-occurrence only when the two accounts' active times overlap by more than c = 12 hours. The paper uses no other rule. Reviewer_oo8n in B said the same.

checkable_claims.claim: There is no ablation of VigDet that uses the prior graph alone (pairwise potentials only).
checkable_claims.evidence: Both ablation variants, VigDet-E and VigDet-PL (lines 256-261), keep the embeddings. Graph-only methods appear only as LPA(CF/TL) in the semi-supervised Table 2 (AP 71.1, 69.7) and as Co-activity and Clickstream in Table 1, which score at chance (AUC 52.5, 53.5).

checkable_claims.claim: Dense-block (Fraudar), temporal-graph-embedding and tensor-factorisation baselines are missing.
checkable_claims.evidence: None of these methods appears in Tables 1-2 or in Section 2. Reviewer_aBu9 made the same request (M-Zoom) and repeated it after the rebuttal.

checkable_claims.claim: Many hashtags of the detected COVID group are Canadian politics, so the method may find groups that are not coordinated.
checkable_claims.evidence: In Figure 3, 11 of the coordinated group's top 30 hashtags are Canadian politics (cdnpoli, onpoli, bcpoli, ableg, abpoli, canada, cdnmedia and four Trudeau tags). VigDet flags 7k of 31k accounts (lines 294-296). Suspended accounts are 4.26% against 3.45% (lines 311-312). One of the four Table 3 tweets is ordinary commentary on O'Toole and Trudeau.

checkable_claims.claim: The paper declares no potential negative societal impacts.
The baseline numbers in Table 1 are lower than those reported in [25].
checkable_claims.evidence: Reference [25] is not in the pair files. The authors replied that the unsupervised numbers match [25] and that only the semi-supervised setting differs from [25]'s supervised one.

rebuttal.evidence: No A review was edited after posting. Reviewer_aBu9 replied on 2021-08-23 and kept 6: 'the rebuttal has partially addressed my concerns, but I believe that some of the important comparisons/ablations are missing'. Reviewer_q2wM, Reviewer_insa and Reviewer_neqB never replied, also after the authors' reminders on 2021-08-31.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: The rebuttal argued and added no experiments. aBu9 rejected its answer that Co-activity, Clickstream and LPA are the graph-only comparison: 'I was referring to an ablation of your proposed method'. aBu9 repeated the dense-block and tensor request. The rebuttal answered coordination against community with an unreported Louvain analysis and the claim that coordinated accounts act in a 'more concerted' way. It refused synthetic data. It corrected neqB's baseline claim and q2wM's ablation claim, but neither reviewer answered.

ac.evidence: Ratings 6, 5, 5, 4 (mean 5.0). The meta-review sets 'three knowledgeable reviewers' who 'indicated ... to reject' against 'one reviewer [with] weak support for acceptance', and lists the union of all concerns. Two of the three have confidence 3, and q2wM wrote 'Without having deep expertise in this area'. It names clarity as a concern, but aBu9 and q2wM praised the clarity. It does not note that the paper answers neqB's baseline claim and q2wM's ablation claim.

main_reasons_for_decision: Three of four ratings below the threshold (5, 5, 4), none moved after the rebuttal; mean 5.0
Missing comparisons: dense-block and tensor baselines (insa, aBu9), a graph-only VigDet (aBu9), a run without AMDN-HAGE initialisation (neqB)
No evidence that the method separates coordinated accounts from ordinary communities (aBu9, insa; the AC's requested revision)
Incremental over AMDN-HAGE [25] with shallow priors: an unexplained cube and one 12-hour overlap rule (q2wM, insa, neqB)

outlier.evidence: The only score below the threshold, two points under three 7s. Its reason is accurate but thin: the method 'only incorporate[s] filtered co-activity matrix' into the AMDN-HAGE embedding (Section 4.1, line 147), and Section 4.2 is hard to follow. Reviewer_P6ya also called the work incremental. The main review is three sentences and says nothing about the experiments. w5yn did not answer the rebuttal or the reminder of 2021-08-31, and the AC did not mention it.

inattentive_reviews.evidence: Rating 7 after a reported four hours. The main review is three sentences of praise ('interesting', 'solid contributions', 'intuitive') with no question and no weakness; limitations 'N/A'. Its one factual statement is wrong: the authors did not verify the model on the data set they collected. No reply; the authors' answer to it was a thank-you.

checkable_claims.claim: The authors collected a data set and verified the effectiveness of the model on it.
checkable_claims.evidence: Effectiveness is measured only on IRA, which came from the authors of [16] (Checklist 3(a), lines 432-435). The COVID set the authors collected has no labels (lines 290-292).

checkable_claims.claim: Limitations and societal impact are appropriately addressed.
checkable_claims.evidence: Checklist 1(c) declares no negative societal impact ('[Yes] None', line 423). Limitations get two sentences in Checklist 1(b). Reviewer_w5yn in B and Reviewer_insa in A flagged this.

checkable_claims.claim: The core of the prior-knowledge graph construction exists in other works.
checkable_claims.evidence: Section 4.1 builds the graph with co-activity [24] (line 147). The only additions are a cube (Eq. 4) and one overlap rule (Eq. 5).

checkable_claims.claim: The paper includes an ablation study.
checkable_claims.evidence: VigDet-E and VigDet-PL (Tables 1-2). The EM loop, the main technical step, adds +2.1 (CF) and +0.6 (TL) AP over VigDet-E unsupervised, and +0.5 and -0.1 semi-supervised. Most of the gain over AMDN-HAGE + KMeans (82.0) comes from one E-step on the prior graph. Error bars are only in the appendix.

checkable_claims.claim: There is no clear reason why the exponent in Eq. 4 is three.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 156-158 say only that the cube will 'enlarge the difference'. Reviewer_q2wM in A asked the same question.

checkable_claims.claim: The claim that E-step belief propagation 'converges at an optimal solution' needs a proof for this model.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 197-198 assert it by citing [12, 10] and give no proof. Mean-field updates on a dense, loopy graph reach a fixed point, not in general an optimum.

checkable_claims.claim: A good number of baselines were used on the IRA dataset.
checkable_claims.evidence: Six unsupervised and seven semi-supervised baselines (Tables 1-2). But the two prior-graph unsupervised baselines score at chance (AUC 52.5, 53.5), and no dense-block or tensor method is included.

rebuttal.evidence: Reviewer_P6ya edited on 2021-08-16 and added 'The authors have clarified my main issues' and 'this paper should move forward'. Whether its 7 was a raise is not visible. Reviewer_oo8n edited on 2021-08-24: 'I will stick with my positive rating.' Reviewer_w5yn (5) and Reviewer_hg1U (7) never edited or replied.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: P6ya accepted two explanations: the cube with normalisation removes low-weight edges, and new prior rules can cover URL sharing and cross-platform coordination. oo8n accepted promises of a formal convergence proof in the supplement and of the exponent as a hyperparameter. The rebuttal added no experiments. w5yn got a restatement of the method and did not reply.

ac.evidence: Ratings 5, 7, 7, 7 (mean 6.5). The three-sentence meta-review opens with oo8n's summary almost word for word ('a method for detecting groups of coordinated social media accounts which are engaged in misinformation campaigns') and echoes oo8n's 'reasonable' and 'generally solid'. It says 'All the reviewers' found the application important and the evaluation solid; w5yn said neither. It names no weakness.

main_reasons_for_decision: Three 7s: an important application and a principled mix of a neural TPP and a prior-knowledge graph (P6ya, oo8n)
Experiments judged solid, with many baselines, an ablation and a 'compelling' COVID case study (oo8n, P6ya)
Known limits (cube, single temporal rule, one labelled dataset) treated as future work, not grounds to reject (oo8n, P6ya)
Incremental novelty accepted as 'not groundbreaking' (AC, P6ya)
The rebuttal satisfied P6ya on the cubic weighting and on other forms of coordination

issues_only_a: Missing dense-block, tensor-factorisation and temporal-graph-embedding baselines such as Fraudar and M-Zoom (insa, aBu9)
No evidence that the method separates coordination from ordinary communities; the COVID group's hashtags are largely Canadian politics (aBu9, insa)
No run without AMDN-HAGE initialisation and no supervised setting (neqB)
No synthetic experiments, for example with an SBM (insa)
Thin COVID data description: no keywords, dates, topic-mining method or news-source list (insa)
Power-law sparsity named as the motivation but not shown to be addressed (aBu9)
issues_only_b: Section 4.2 is hard to follow and the intuition for Eq. 6 is unclear (w5yn); A's aBu9 and q2wM called the paper clear
No proof that the E-step converges to an optimum or of what Theorem 1 implies for VBEM (oo8n)
An adversary could evade the single temporal-logic rule (oo8n)
Other forms of coordination (URL sharing, copy-paste, cross-platform) may be missed (P6ya)
Possible demographic bias (oo8n); an overview figure is needed (P6ya)
shared_issues: Incremental over AMDN-HAGE [25] (A: q2wM, insa, neqB; B: w5yn, P6ya)
The cubic exponent is unexplained (A: q2wM; B: P6ya, oo8n)
The temporal-logic prior is one simple rule (A: q2wM; B: oo8n)
Only one labelled dataset (A: neqB; B: oo8n)
No discussion of negative societal impact (A: insa, q2wM, neqB, aBu9; B: w5yn, oo8n)
Figures 2 and 3 are hard to read (A: q2wM, insa; B: P6ya)
verdict: Both committees saw the same moderate paper and set a different bar. VigDet adds a co-activity prior graph to AMDN-HAGE [25], filtered by an unexplained cube or one 12-hour overlap rule, and has labels on one dataset. Both committees named these limits. B's two detailed reviewers, P6ya and oo8n, still gave 7 for an important application and a principled model, and B's AC repeated oo8n. A's reviewers wanted dense-block and tensor baselines, a graph-only ablation and proof that the method finds coordination rather than communities. The paper confirms those gaps: no such baselines, chance-level prior-graph baselines (AUC 52.5, 53.5), and a COVID 'coordinated' group of 7k of 31k accounts with Canadian-politics hashtags. Each side also had weak reviews. Two A detractors made claims the paper contradicts and never answered the rebuttal; B's hg1U gave a three-sentence 7. Neither flips its side: without neqB A's mean is 5.33, and without hg1U B's is 6.33. Nobody found a technical error.
candidate_reasons: Dense-block baselines demanded by one committee
